# The generic gamma_d times selected-mass transfer is false

A tempting strengthening of the fixed-mass moment-body approach is:
for a weighted integer center j and 0<t<=D_j, the ordinary centroid of
the base-balanced mass-t moment body has unnormalized halfspace depth
at least gamma_d t. The following exact convex-body example disproves
that strengthening. It does not disprove the fixed choice t=M/2^n or OC.

Let n=d=1 and let C be the convex hull of the three interval fibers

    C_0=[0,4],  C_1=[2,16],  C_2=[7,11].

The Minkowski midpoint of the endpoint intervals is [7/2,15/2], contained
in the middle interval. Hence these are exactly the integer fibers of C.
The body is a compact full-dimensional polygon. Its mixed length is
M=4+14+4=22, and the marginal closed-halfspace capacity at j=1 is
D_j=18. In particular j is a weighted integer centerpoint.

Take t=18. Base balance forces the endpoint selected masses to be equal.
The mass-t continuous moment interval B_t(1) has exact endpoints

    L=19/3,       U=1873/216.                         (1)

For the upper endpoint, select the portions above the affine thresholds

    x >= 5/6+(7/2)z.

Their masses are (19/6,35/3,19/6), summing to 18 and having base mean 1.
Their total continuous first moment is 1873/12; division by 18 gives U.
Optimality follows by the threshold exchange inequality. For every other
feasible density f, integration of

    [x-5/6-(7/2)z](1_H-f) >=0

cancels the mass and base moments and proves that this selection maximizes
the continuous moment.

For the lower endpoint, select the full endpoint intervals and [2,12]
on the middle fiber. This is the portion below

    x <= 12+(7/2)(z-1).

It has masses (4,10,4), total mass 18, base mean 1, and continuous first
moment 8+70+36=114. The same exchange argument with reversed orientation
proves its minimality, giving L=114/18=19/3. Compact convexity of the
feasible density class shows that (1) describes the whole interval.

Its ordinary centroid is therefore

    y=(L+U)/2=3241/432.

Consider the closed ambient halfspace

    H={ (z,x):x >= y+(1513/432)(z-1) }.

It contains (1,y). At z=0 its threshold is 4, so the left contribution
is one endpoint of length zero. At z=2 its threshold is 2377/216>11,
so the right contribution is empty. The middle contribution is

    mu(H)=16-y=3671/432 < 9 = gamma_1 t.

The exact deficit is 217/432. Every measure used here is H_1 on the
actual interval fibers, and the halfspace is closed and oblique.

The OC target in this example is M/4=11/2, which is smaller than the
exhibited cap mass. Also t=18 differs from the fixed half-mass t=11.
Thus the conclusion is confined to failure of the generic selected-mass
transfer theorem stated at the start.
